nodes.title: Constitution
bullets: Part III sets out Fundamental Rights.
Read guarantees alongside their limits and remedies.
nodes.mains: Begin with the constitutional guarantee, then test the restriction.

nodes.title: Fundamental Rights
bullets: Identify the right-holder, duty-bearer and guarantee.
Distinguish a restriction from a violation.
Finish with enforcement and an appropriate remedy.
nodes.mains: Right → restriction → justification → remedy.

nodes.title: Article 12
bullets: Identifies bodies covered by “State” in Part III.
The definition includes government and local or other authorities.
nodes.mains: Identify who owes the constitutional obligation.

nodes.title: Article 13
bullets: Inconsistent laws are void to the extent of inconsistency.
Constitutional amendments have a distinct framework under Article 368.
nodes.mains: Identify the law and the precise right it abridges.

nodes.title: Article 14
bullets: Protects every person.
Pairs equality before law with equal protection of laws.
nodes.mains: Ask whether different treatment has a defensible constitutional basis.

nodes.title: Article 15
bullets: Protects citizens against specified grounds of discrimination.
Clauses permit specified special provisions, including for women and children.
nodes.mains: Distinguish prohibited discrimination from measures advancing substantive equality.

nodes.title: Article 16
bullets: Guarantees citizens equality of opportunity in public employment.
Reservation-related clauses have distinct requirements.
nodes.mains: Keep public employment separate from educational admission.

nodes.title: Article 17
bullets: Abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice.
Enforcement of resulting disabilities is an offence punishable by law.
nodes.mains: Connect social equality with effective enforcement.

nodes.title: Article 18
bullets: The State cannot confer titles except military or academic distinctions.
Rules concerning foreign titles and benefits vary by citizenship and office.
nodes.mains: Distinguish prohibited titles from permitted distinctions.

nodes.title: Article 19
bullets: Includes expression, assembly, association, movement, residence and profession.
Each freedom has its own constitutionally specified restrictions.
nodes.mains: Name the freedom and its relevant restriction clause; avoid a generic public-interest claim.

nodes.title: Article 20
bullets: Protects against retrospective criminal punishment and double jeopardy.
An accused cannot be compelled to be a witness against themselves.
nodes.mains: Separate the three safeguards instead of treating them as interchangeable.

nodes.title: Article 21
bullets: Protects every person.
Deprivation must follow a legally valid procedure.
nodes.mains: Start with liberty, examine the procedure, then connect the relevant judicial interpretation.

nodes.title: Article 21A
bullets: Requires free and compulsory education for children aged six to fourteen.
The manner of provision is determined by law.
nodes.mains: Connect the guarantee to access and implementation barriers.

nodes.title: Article 22
bullets: Ordinary arrest protections include information, counsel and production before a magistrate.
Preventive detention follows a separate constitutional framework.
nodes.mains: Distinguish ordinary arrest safeguards from preventive-detention rules.

nodes.title: Article 23
bullets: Prohibits trafficking, begar and similar forced labour.
Compulsory public service is subject to the stated non-discrimination condition.
nodes.mains: Connect coercion and vulnerability with enforcement.

nodes.title: Article 24
bullets: Bars employment of children below fourteen in factories, mines or other hazardous employment.
Broader statutory protection must be distinguished from this constitutional text.
nodes.mains: Link protection from exploitation to education and social support.

nodes.title: Article 25
bullets: Protects all persons, subject to public order, morality, health and other Part III provisions.
Preserves specified regulatory and social-reform powers.
nodes.mains: State both the guarantee and its express limitations.

nodes.title: Article 26
bullets: Protects denominational religious affairs and related institutional interests.
Subject to public order, morality and health.
nodes.mains: Distinguish individual conscience from denominational autonomy.

nodes.title: Article 27
bullets: Bars compulsion to pay taxes specifically appropriated to promote or maintain a particular religion.
Read the provision’s specific tax-purpose requirement.
nodes.mains: Avoid equating every religion-related expenditure with an Article 27 violation.

nodes.title: Article 28
bullets: Rules differ by state maintenance, administration, recognition and aid.
The article includes an endowment exception and consent safeguards.
nodes.mains: Identify the type of institution before applying the rule.

nodes.title: Article 29
bullets: Protects a section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture.
Clause (2) addresses admission discrimination in state-maintained or aided institutions.
nodes.mains: Do not assume every Article 29 protection is confined to minorities.

nodes.title: Article 30
bullets: Religious and linguistic minorities may establish and administer educational institutions.
State aid cannot discriminate merely on minority management.
nodes.mains: Connect cultural autonomy with educational governance.

nodes.title: Article 31
bullets: Article 31 was omitted by the 44th Amendment.
The constitutional property guarantee is now in Article 300A, outside Part III.
nodes.mains: Do not describe property as a current Fundamental Right.

nodes.title: Article 31A
bullets: Protects specified categories of laws against Articles 14 and 19 challenges, subject to conditions.
Read the listed categories and provisos.
nodes.mains: Identify the exact constitutional protection before claiming immunity.

nodes.title: Article 31B
bullets: Concerns listed Acts and Regulations.
Under I. R. Coelho (2007), Ninth Schedule insertions on or after 24 April 1973 remain subject to basic-structure review.
nodes.mains: Do not assume a Ninth Schedule entry ends all constitutional scrutiny.

nodes.title: Article 31C
bullets: Operative protection concerns laws giving effect to Article 39(b) or (c).
The 2024 edition records judicial invalidation of the attempted extension to all DPSPs.
nodes.mains: Specify the directive principle and avoid claiming blanket immunity for all welfare laws.

nodes.title: Article 32
bullets: Guarantees access to the Supreme Court to enforce Part III rights.
The Court can issue appropriate directions, orders and writs.
nodes.mains: End with the enforceable right and the remedy sought.

nodes.title: Article 33
bullets: Parliament may modify rights for specified forces and related services.
The purpose is proper discharge of duties and maintenance of discipline.
nodes.mains: State the institutional context and constitutional purpose of modification.

nodes.title: Article 34
bullets: Parliament may provide indemnity and validate specified acts in a martial-law area.
This is distinct from the emergency provisions.
nodes.mains: Keep martial law and constitutional emergency analytically separate.

nodes.title: Article 35
bullets: Reserves lawmaking on specified Part III matters to Parliament.
Includes matters referred to in Articles 16(3), 32(3), 33 and 34.
nodes.mains: Identify legislative competence as well as the substantive right.

nodes.title: Directive Principles
bullets: Article 37 distinguishes non-enforceability from their fundamental role in governance.
Article 31C concerns specified connections to Article 39(b) and (c).
nodes.mains: Examine how rights and policy goals can be pursued together.

nodes.title: Article 226
bullets: High Courts can issue writs for Fundamental Rights and for other purposes.
nodes.mains: Distinguish the scope of Article 226 from Article 32.

nodes.title: Article 359
bullets: A Presidential order can suspend access to courts for specified rights during an emergency.
Articles 20 and 21 are excluded from this power.
nodes.mains: Distinguish the right from the ability to move a court to enforce it.

nodes.title: Substantive equality
bullets: Formal equal treatment and corrective measures answer different problems.
Article 15 contains specific enabling provisions.
nodes.mains: Explain how a targeted measure advances equality, then examine its design.
nodes.relationNote: Editorial application; not an independent constitutional article.

nodes.title: Privacy
bullets: Privacy is protected within Part III.
Restrictions require constitutional justification.
nodes.mains: Identify the intrusion, its purpose and the safeguards against disproportionate interference.

nodes.title: Maneka Gandhi (1978)
bullets: Article 21 procedure must be fair, just and reasonable.
Read Articles 14, 19 and 21 together where applicable.
nodes.mains: Use Maneka Gandhi (1978) to connect procedural fairness with liberty and equality.
nodes.fullTitle: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
nodes.locator: Puttaswamy (2017), Chandrachud J., para 23, PDF pp. 22–23: discussion of Maneka Gandhi
nodes.status: Historical holding; supported here by later Supreme Court discussion.

nodes.title: Puttaswamy (2017)
bullets: The nine-judge Bench recognised constitutional protection for privacy.
Privacy is not absolute; restrictions need justification.
nodes.mains: In Puttaswamy (2017), the Supreme Court recognised privacy as a fundamental right.
nodes.fullTitle: Justice K. S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) and Another v. Union of India and Others
nodes.locator: Order of the Court; Chandrachud J., para 325
nodes.status: 2017 privacy ruling; distinguish it from the 2018 Aadhaar decision.

nodes.title: Electoral Bonds (2024)
bullets: Non-disclosure provisions violated Article 19(1)(a).
Unlimited corporate contributions were held arbitrary under Article 14.
nodes.mains: Use the 2024 electoral-bonds judgment to connect transparency, equality and democratic accountability.
nodes.fullTitle: Association for Democratic Reforms and Another v. Union of India and Others
nodes.status: Dated judgment example; not a live current-affairs feed.

nodes.title: Funding disclosure
bullets: The 2024 judgment directed disclosure of electoral-bond funding information.
This is a dated application of constitutional scrutiny.
nodes.mains: Connect a concrete funding-disclosure example to the voter’s right to information.
nodes.status: Historical current-affairs example, preserved with its date.

nodes.title: Article 31D
bullets: Omitted by the 43rd Amendment.
Included for historical orientation, not as an operative provision.
nodes.mains: Distinguish historical restrictions from the current constitutional framework.

nodes.title: Article 32A
bullets: Omitted by the 43rd Amendment.
Included for historical orientation, not as an operative provision.
nodes.mains: Distinguish historical restrictions from the current constitutional framework.

edges.label: contains
edges.explanation: Part III of the Constitution sets out Fundamental Rights.

edges.label: contains
edges.explanation: Part III includes Article 31. It is omitted in the current text.

edges.label: read together
edges.explanation: The discussion of Maneka Gandhi connects equality with fair procedure and liberty.

edges.label: read together
edges.explanation: Article 19 scrutiny remains relevant where a measure also affects liberty.

edges.label: interpreted by
edges.explanation: Maneka Gandhi requires a fair, just and reasonable procedure.

edges.label: interpreted by
edges.explanation: The Court located privacy in life and liberty and the freedoms of Part III.

edges.label: recognises
edges.explanation: The nine-judge ruling recognises the constitutional right to privacy.

edges.label: applied in
edges.explanation: The non-disclosure provisions were invalidated under Article 19(1)(a).

edges.label: applied in
edges.explanation: The unlimited corporate-contribution amendment was invalidated under Article 14.

edges.label: directed
edges.explanation: Paragraph 217 directs funding disclosure to give effect to the ruling.

edges.label: illustrates
edges.explanation: Special provisions under Article 15 help explain substantive equality.

edges.label: compare
edges.explanation: Compare general equality with targeted measures under Article 15.

edges.label: compare remedies
edges.explanation: Article 226 extends to Fundamental Rights and other purposes; Article 32 concerns Part III enforcement.

edges.label: specified protection
edges.explanation: Operative Article 31C protection concerns Article 39(b) and (c), not all DPSPs.

edges.label: complements
edges.explanation: Education and protection from hazardous child employment can support one another in a Mains analysis.

edges.label: historical provision
edges.explanation: The current Part III text records Article 31D as omitted by the 43rd Amendment.

edges.label: historical provision
edges.explanation: The current Part III text records Article 32A as omitted by the 43rd Amendment.
